title: Partition List
statement_short: Given the head of a linked list and a value x, partition it such that all nodes less than x come before nodes greater than or equal to x. Preserve the original relative order of the nodes in each of the two partitions.
hint: Small node count (<= 200) allows creating two dummy chain lists to separate and combine nodes in O(n) time.
keywords: nodes less than x come before
why_not: Right: Two Pointers builds two separate sub-lists ('less' and 'greater_or_equal') and stitches them together in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not Sorting: General sorting algorithms reorder node values but violate the requirement to preserve original relative order. Not Stack: Pushing nodes onto stacks reorganizes nodes but uses extra O(n) space and reverses sub-list order. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Hash tables do not assist with stable sequence partitioning.
